newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO steady to soft as crude eases.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO steady to soft as crude eases.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Thursday were expected to end steady to shade softer from Wednesday as buyers remained sidelined by current firm prices, traders said.
They said prices are likely to hover between $120-$124 per tonne. Prices on Wednesday were indicated at $120-$123 per tonne.
Traders said prices have risen in tandem with the recent gain in crude prices but fundamentals in the physical market were still lagging behind.
"I have hardly heard of any Chinese demand," said a trader.
"Current prices may ease as crude prices soften," said another trader.
Some distressed supplies were still unsold from South Korea, he said.
In the swaps market, October fuel oil was discussed at $121.50/$122 within's Wednesday's $120.25/$121.50
